fullPassage:
Wheels of Adventures

A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling!"

Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.

Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the famous spot that appears in most movies and TV shows filmed in San Francisco. We took a cruise, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset.

The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery gradually changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to fuel up for a hike.

While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.

Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now." That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture!

Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led us to green fields and streams where we saw some wildlife. Watching people floating down the Merced River and hiking the Half Dome was cool. It was indeed a wonderful trip, with lots of laughter, joy, and sweat.

I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.

questions.passage: Fisherman's Wharf is (A)[popular / unpopular] for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were (B)[hungry / full], but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a (C)[roasted / frozen] crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Fisherman's Wharf는 예쁜 가게와 해산물 식당으로 인기 있다(popular). 우리는 배가 고팠지만(hungry) 점심 메뉴를 고르는 데 거의 한 시간이 걸렸다. 우리는 구운(roasted) 게와 클램차우더를 먹기로 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② popular — hungry — roasted: 원문 그대로
❌ ① unpopular(인기 없는): 예쁜 가게와 식당이 많다는 맥락에 반대
❌ ③ full(배부른): 음식을 고르는 맥락에서 배가 부르면 모순
❌ ④ unpopular + full: 두 단어 모두 문맥 반대
det.tip: popular(인기 있는) ↔ unpopular(인기 없는), hungry(배고픈) ↔ full(배부른), roasted(구운) ↔ frozen(냉동된)

questions.passage: Our hike took a (A)[dangerous / safe] turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had (B)[packed / unpacked] because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy (C)[grabbed / released] a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 하이킹이 한 지점에서 위험한(dangerous) 방향으로 전환되었다. 우리가 싸온(packed) 음식 냄새를 맡았기 때문이다. Roy 삼촌이 돌을 집어(grabbed) 던졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ dangerous — packed — grabbed: 원문 그대로
❌ ① safe(안전한): 곰을 만난 '위험한' 상황에서 '안전한'은 모순
❌ ② unpacked(풀어놓은): 음식을 '싸왔다'는 맥락에서 반대
❌ ③ safe + unpacked + released(놓아주다): 모두 문맥 반대
det.tip: dangerous(위험한) ↔ safe(안전한), packed(싸온) ↔ unpacked(풀어놓은), grab(잡다) ↔ release(놓다)

det.korean: 물론 나에게는 소중한(valuable) 추억도 있다. 나는 깊은 숨(breath)을 들이쉬고 새로운 세계로 뛰어들어 도전에 맞섰다(faced).
det.analysis:

❌ ③ forced(강제했다): 강제는 설득과 다름. 자발성 없는 행동
❌ ④ allowed(허락했다): 허락은 설득보다 소극적인 행위
det.tip: persuade = convince. 둘 다 '논리/감정으로 설득하다'. force(강제하다)와 구별

questions.passage:
Wheels of Adventures

A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling! "

Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off. 

Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the famous spot that appears in most movies and TV shows filmed in San Francisco. We took a cruise, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset. 

The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery <u>gradually</u> changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 gradually와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 풍경이 도시에서 교외, 숲, 산으로 서서히(gradually) 바뀌는 것을 보았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② little by little(조금씩): gradually와 동의어, 점진적 변화
❌ ① suddenly(갑자기): gradually의 반의어
❌ ③ rapidly(빠르게): 서서히와 반대되는 속도
❌ ④ completely(완전히): 정도의 부사이지 속도의 부사가 아님
det.tip: gradually(서서히) = little by little = step by step. city→suburb→forest→mountain 단계적 변화가 단서

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 disappointed와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 케이블카가 휠체어 사용자를 수용하지 않는다는 것을 알고 실망했다(disappointed).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ thrilled(매우 기뻐하는): disappointed(실망한)의 반의어
❌ ① frustrated(좌절한): disappointed와 유사한 의미
❌ ② upset(속상한): disappointed와 유사한 의미
❌ ④ concerned(걱정하는): 반의어가 아닌 다른 부정적 감정
det.tip: disappointed(실망한) ↔ thrilled(매우 기뻐하는) / delighted / pleased. 감정 반의어 시험 빈출

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 kindly와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: Roy 삼촌이 친절하게(kindly) 공원까지 태워다 주었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ harshly(거칠게, 가혹하게): kindly(친절하게)의 반의어
❌ ① generously(관대하게): kindly와 유사한 의미
❌ ② willingly(기꺼이): kindly와 유사한 뉘앙스
❌ ③ gently(부드럽게): kindly와 유사한 의미
det.tip: kindly(친절하게) ↔ harshly(거칠게, 가혹하게) / rudely(무례하게). 부사 반의어는 형용사 반의어와 함께 학습

questions.passage:
(A) As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips because it began to <u>approach</u> us.

(B) The city decided to <u>approach</u> the traffic problem by building more bike lanes and improving public transportation.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 approach의 의미를 바르게 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 곰이 우리에게 다가오기(approach) 시작했다 — (B) 도시가 교통 문제를 접근하기로(approach) 결정했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 다가오다(물리적 이동) — (B) 접근하다(문제 해결 방식): approach의 두 가지 의미
❌ ① (A) 접근법은 명사 의미로 동사 문맥에 부적합
❌ ② 둘 다 '접근하다'로 번역하면 물리적 이동 vs 방법론 차이가 드러나지 않음
❌ ④ (B) 도달하다(reach)는 approach의 의미와 다름
det.tip: approach: ① (자동사/타동사) 물리적으로 다가오다 ② (타동사) 문제에 접근하다/다루다 ③ (명사) 접근법. 문맥에 따라 의미 구분 필수

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to meet or come upon someone or something unexpectedly"

det.korean: "누군가 또는 무엇인가를 예상치 못하게 만나다" → encounter(마주치다)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ encounter(마주치다): 영영풀이와 정확히 일치. unexpectedly가 핵심
❌ ① approach(다가오다): 만나는 것이 아니라 다가가는 것
❌ ② organize(정리하다): 만남과 무관
❌ ③ assure(안심시키다): 만남과 무관
det.tip: encounter = meet unexpectedly. 본문에서 'we encountered a black bear'(곰을 우연히 마주쳤다)와 연결

questions.passage: The sea lions __________ (peace) lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 바다사자들이 평화롭게(peacefully) 부표 위에 누워 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ peacefully: 부사 위치(lying 수식). peace(명사) → peaceful(형용사) → peacefully(부사)
❌ peaceful: 형용사로 동사 lying을 수식할 수 없음
❌ peacefulness: 명사로 부사 자리에 부적합
det.tip: peace(명사, 평화) → peaceful(형용사, 평화로운) → peacefully(부사, 평화롭게). 동사(lying) 앞 부사 자리

questions.passage: Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was __________ (fortune) to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: Dan과 Roy 삼촌 같은 동행이 있어서 다행이었다(fortunate).
det.analysis:
✅ fortunate: 'I was ____ to have ~' 구조에서 보어 역할 형용사. fortune(명사) → fortunate(형용사)
❌ fortunately: 부사로 보어 자리에 부적합 (I was fortunately는 비문)
❌ fortune: 명사로 'I was fortune'은 비문
det.tip: fortune(명사, 운/행운) → fortunate(형용사, 운이 좋은) → fortunately(부사, 다행히). 'be + 형용사 + to V' 구문이 단서

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 점심시간에 도착하여 하이킹을 위해 에너지를 보충하려고(fuel up) 거대한 햄버거를 먹었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① fuel up(에너지를 보충하다): 하이킹 전 큰 햄버거를 먹는 맥락. 활동 전 에너지 충전
❌ ② give up(포기하다): 하이킹을 위한 준비 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ slow down(속도를 줄이다): 에너지 보충과 무관
❌ ④ break down(고장나다/무너지다): 문맥과 완전히 무관
det.tip: fuel up(에너지를 보충하다) — 연료(fuel)를 채우다에서 유래. 음식을 먹고 에너지를 충전한다는 비유적 표현

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 이미 미래에 다음 여행을 기대하고(looking forward to) 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② looking forward to(기대하다): 여행 전체를 긍정적으로 회고하며 다음 여행을 기대하는 결말 맥락
❌ ① giving up on(포기하다): 용기를 갖고 도전했다는 결론에 반대
❌ ③ running away from(도망치다): 새로운 세계로 뛰어들었다는 맥락에 반대
❌ ④ falling behind in(뒤처지다): 여행의 긍정적 결말과 무관
det.tip: look forward to + 명사/동명사 (기대하다). 'already'가 강한 기대감의 단서. 글 전체의 긍정적 메시지와 연결
